LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines `source`, `md5sums`, `sha256sums`, and variables (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, etc.) in the top-level scope with no command substitution or side effects. Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` only parses/subsources the PKGBUILD (top-level scope + `pkgver()`), and `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` additionally fetches and extracts the archive but stops before `prepare()`/`build()`/`package()`.

The `source` array fetches a tarball from `https://cpan.metacpan.org/authors/id/P/PE/PETDANCE/$pkgname-v$pkgver.tar.gz`, which is the project's own upstream (CPAN/Perl.org). No checksum is set to `SKIP`; both `md5sums` and `sha256sums` are fully pinned. There is no `pkgver()` function defined (version is hardcoded), so no code runs there.

No `eval`, `base64`, `curl|wget`, obfuscated strings, or unexpected file/network operations appear in the top-level scope or source/packaging declarations. The functions that could contain dangerous behavior (`build()`, `check()`, `package()`) are explicitly out of scope for this gate since `--nobuild`/`--noprepare` prevent their execution.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>

Clean PKGBUILD; sources fetch is standard and safe.</summary>
